newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PMZ mum on Heinz plant sale.
newsitem.headline: Czech PMZ mum on Heinz plant sale.

text.p: The largest Czech infant food manufacturer, Heinz-PMZ a.s., said on Monday that it would not comment until Tuesday at the earliest about U.S.-based H.J. Heinz's plan to sell its 80 percent stake in the plant.
A Prague public relations firm representing the company, based in the eastern Czech town of Zabreh na Morave, said a spokesman might be available to speak on the subject on Tuesday.

The Pittsburgh-based food group Heinz said on Friday it would close or sell at least 25 plants, cut 2,500 jobs worldwide and take a $650 million pre-tax charge to cover the costs of a massive corporate reorganisation.
It named the Czech PMZ plant, which under communism was the country's primary producer of baby formula, as one that should be sold.
Heinz said its intention was to focus on expanding its global leadership in high-margin ketchup and condiments, tuna products and weight-control and other pre-packaged foods.
Heinz bought the freshly-privatised PMZ stake in 1995 saying it was part of a concerted strategy to double sales in former-communist Eastern Europe, mostly through baby food sales.
The PMZ plant produced 65 million litres of dried milk in 1996, according to the Czech news agency CTK, down from 100 million litres in the previous year.
PMZ said it would either break even or make a moderate profit in 1996, after an 88 million crown loss in 1995.
